findings.source_passage: There now's a patched professor in Queen Nature's granite-founded College; but methinks he's too subservient. Where wert thou born?
findings.why_it_matters: The draft preserves the line but drops the reply 'Excellent! Thou'st hit the world by that' and 'I know not, sir, but I was born there,' which set up Ahab's wordplay on Man/man. Without that exchange the rhetorical build to 'The dead, blind wall butts all inquiring heads at last' loses its comic and philosophical scaffolding.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the two short exchanges ('Excellent! Thou'st hit the world by that' / 'I know not, sir, but I was born there') so the Man/man wordplay sequence is intact.

findings.source_passage: Pip? whom call ye Pip? Pip jumped from the whale-boat. Pip's missing. Let's see now if ye haven't fished him up here, fisherman. It drags hard; I guess he's holding on.
findings.source_locator: Pip's first speech after the line snaps
findings.why_it_matters: Pip's dissociated third-person ravings are among the most critically noted passages in the chapter; the draft collapses them into a single authorial summary ('Pip came babbling, speaking of himself in the third person'), erasing the hallucinatory voice that defines his madness.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore Pip's verbatim speech in full or nearly full, including 'A hatchet! a hatchet! cut it off—we haul in no cowards here,' since the grotesque imagery is part of the signature.

findings.source_passage: Who art thou, boy? I see not my reflection in the vacant pupils of thy eyes. Oh God! that man should be a thing for immortal souls to sieve through!
findings.source_locator: Ahab's speech after 'Hands off from that holiness'
findings.why_it_matters: 'that man should be a thing for immortal souls to sieve through' is one of the most critically cited lines in the chapter—an interpretive crux on Pip's spiritual transparency—and it is absent from the draft entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full sentence: 'Oh God! that man should be a thing for immortal souls to sieve through!' immediately after 'I see not my reflection in the vacant pupils of thy eyes.'

findings.source_passage: Here's the end of the rotten line—all dripping, too. Mend it, eh? I think we had best have a new line altogether. I'll see Mr. Stubb about it.
findings.why_it_matters: The Manxman's closing coda about the 'rotten line' is the chapter's ironic punctuation—the physical line as metaphor for everything fraying aboard the Pequod. The draft cuts it to 'One daft with strength, the other daft with weakness,' losing the emblematic final image.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the Manxman's full closing remark about the rotten line and his intention to see Stubb about a new one.

summary: The draft's greatest failure is paraphrasing Pip's signature dissociated speech into authorial summary and dropping Ahab's 'immortal souls to sieve through' line, two medium-severity losses that together with the truncated Manxman coda cross the regeneration threshold.
